name: Easy Pressure Cooker Spicy Korean Stew (Jjigae) with Beef, Silken Tofu & Kimchi

instructions.primary_message: Drain kimchi (reserving the liquid for the next step), then roughly chop. Place in a 6-quart electric pressure cooker, along with beef and crushed red pepper (reduce red pepper if a less spicy stew is desired).
instructions.secondary_message:
3 cups kimchi
1 lb beef for stew
½ tsp crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add water, soy sauce, garlic, and a ½-cup of the reserved kimchi liquid to the pressure cooker (if you have less than a 1/2-cup kimchi liquid, add additional water to make up the difference; if you have more than a 1/2-cup, discard extra or reserve for another use). Stir to combine, then lock lid and set pressure to cook on HIGH for 10 minutes. Once done, drape a clean towel over the vent, then manually release pressure.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tbsp soy sauce
2 tsp minced garlic

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, wash, dry, trim, and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Place in a small bowl and set aside.
Halve tofu lengthwise, then cut crosswise into ½-inch thick pieces. (If silken tofu is unavailable, medium or firm tofu are good substitutes but will give a different overall texture to the stew.)

When the stew is done, add green onion and tofu to the pressure cooker, then gently stir to combine. Set to sauté on HIGH and continue to cook until tofu is warmed through, 3-4 minutes more. Remove from heat.

Meanwhile, working in batches, place rice pouches in the microwave, seam-side up. Heat on high for 3-4 minutes (until pouch balloons up with steam for 30 seconds). Allow steam to vent before opening pouch. (Alternatively, rice can be heated in a saucepan according to package instructions.)
instructions.secondary_message: 2 (10 oz) pouch frozen jasmine rice, pre-cooked

instructions.primary_message: To serve, divide rice and kimchi stew between bowls. Enjoy!
